entry.content:

The npm @enspirit/elo package contains a critical sandbox escape vulnerability (CVE-2026-44267) allowing unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary Node.js or browser JavaScript code by exploiting unfiltered `.constructor` member access in the Elo language parser and emitter. An attacker controlling input to `defaultFormats.elo.parse()`, the `bin/elo` CLI tool, or the online playground can craft payloads using `.constructor.constructor` chains to compile directly into `Function` invocations, completely bypassing the language's intended sandboxing. This vulnerability is critical severity; no evidence of active wild exploitation is mentioned but the attack requires only string control, making it highly exploitable. Developers using Elo should immediately update to a patched version once available and avoid processing untrusted Elo code; the online playground should be considered unsafe until patched.

entry.title: imgproxy has integer overflow in imgproxy ICO loader that causes denial of service and may permit remote code execution
entry.content:
vulnerability · integer-overflow

imgproxy ICO image loader contains an integer overflow vulnerability in heap allocation when processing attacker-controlled 32-bit data size values. When data_size exceeds UINT32_MAX minus BMP_FILE_HEADER_LEN, the allocation wraps to a smaller buffer, followed by heap overflow during write operations. This critical vulnerability affects imgproxy v1, v2, and v3, and can be exploited remotely via malicious ICO files to cause denial of service or achieve remote code execution. Immediately patch to the latest patched version; if immediate patching is unavailable, disable or restrict ICO image processing.

Read more · Source: github-advisories

entry.title: New QPACK Flaws Can Crash HTTP/3 Servers, Trigger Up to 4,000-Fold Memory Amplification
entry.content:
vulnerability · dos

HTTP/3 servers using vulnerable QPACK header compression implementations are susceptible to denial-of-service attacks via memory amplification flaws discovered by FoxIO. An unauthenticated remote attacker can crash affected servers by sending specially crafted compressed HTTP headers that expand to consume up to 4,000 times more memory than the original payload, requiring minimal resources from the attacker. This vulnerability is actively exploited in the wild with public proof-of-concept code available. Administrators should immediately patch HTTP/3 server implementations and consider implementing request size limits and rate limiting as interim mitigations until patches are available.

entry.title: Attackers Hijacked Over 300 Tor Exit Relays to Intercept SSH Connections
entry.content:
red-team · man-in-the-middle

Attackers compromised over 300 Tor exit relays in October 2020 to intercept SSH traffic and harvest login credentials from users connecting through those nodes. The attack exploited the trust model of Tor's exit relay network, redirecting SSH connections to attacker-controlled servers that captured passwords before forwarding traffic to legitimate destinations. This represents a high-severity threat to users relying on Tor for secure remote access, though exploitation was limited to SSH password authentication during the five-day window. Users should assume compromised credentials from that period and immediately change SSH passwords; operators should audit exit relay deployments for unauthorized modifications and implement additional monitoring for anomalous SSH traffic patterns.
